analysis.title: One Blackstone Can't Sell $800 Million Of Debt. The Other Just Bought $5 Billion Of Amazon's Data Centers
key_insights: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) agreed to buy a 75% stake in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services owning 13 newly built powered shells (647 MW) in northern Indiana and Mississippi, valuing the portfolio at about $5.0B at a 7.0% initial cap rate (about $385M per building, roughly $7.7M per MW).

Lease terms: triple-net, 12 years initial and up to 32 extended, rent steps up 2.75% a year. Amazon keeps 24.9%, BXDC is managing member, and Amazon keeps approval rights over major decisions. Closing is expected this quarter with a Dec. 31 outside date and a $150M break fee.

Funding is $1.9B from BXDC (essentially all of its IPO proceeds net of fees), $2.5B of new non-recourse mortgages with lender commitments, and $0.6B Amazon's retained stake. Amazon receives up to $4.4B in cash before costs.

Year-one rent is about $350M, rising to about $472M in year 12 (9.4% of today's price). Amazon pays about $4.9B of rent over the initial term against $4.4B of cash received, while Blackstone shareholders keep three quarters of the buildings.

The author argues a AA-rated company renting at 7.0% looks expensive against Goldman's figures of a 5.15% 10-year Treasury and a 6.42% iBoxx investment grade yield, and that 7.0% is the top of BXDC's 5.75%-7.0% buy box. The author notes a cap rate and a coupon are not the same thing.

Goldman credit data cited: AI-related IG issuer spreads at roughly 140bps against under 100bps for other issuers. Goldman's 'The Credit Line: From Shell to Compute' raised its 2027 AI project finance issuance forecast to $545B from $300B ($225B shells, $320B chips). 2026 to date: $80B of IG and junk data center bonds, $22B non-syndicated construction loans, $48B compute financing.

The author reads the deal as debt moving from the corporate bond market into structured formats (sale-leaseback joint ventures), the same template as Meta's Hyperion with Blue Owl. BXDC chief Nick Pell called the hyperscaler sale-leaseback channel a doubling of the total addressable market.

BXDC IPO'd in May at $20, raising just over $2.0B. It reports zero revenue, $1.96B of cash and $28.2M of interest income. It closed Friday at $16.69 against cash of $19.48 a share, and rose about 6% premarket to about $17.70.

The author's estimate of equity economics: 75.1% share of rent less interest at a 6.42% mortgage rate, less a 1% fee, gives about $1.17 a share, a 6.6% yield on $17.70 (5.8% on $20). Each 50bps on the mortgage rate is worth about 9 cents a share. If lenders demand around 245bps over Treasuries, as QTS paid, debt cost would exceed the buildings' yield.
Blackstone waived management and incentive fees through Nov. 15 and now collects 1% of market cap a year, about $18M. The $2.5B of mortgages BXDC needs is five times the amount QTS could not place.
QTS, Blackstone's data center developer, raised only $300M of an $800M private placement. The author says insurers and asset managers told QTS they were full.

Portfolio is over two thirds northern Indiana by value, the rest Mississippi, states not among those pursuing data center pauses (Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Michigan). A JPMorgan report from May said over 60% of 2027 planned capacity had not broken ground.
The author speculates, without confirmation, that the shells may be part of Amazon's Project Rainier campus built for Anthropic, which prices an IPO on Wednesday night.
The author's conclusion is that finished, leased, guaranteed buildings find buyers while development risk does not, and that Amazon selling is not bullish since the AI buildout runs on debt.

market_movers.rationale: Stock rose about 6% premarket to about $17.70 on the Amazon deal but remains about 11% below the $20 IPO price. The author estimates a 6.6% yield and warns debt costs near 245bps over Treasuries would reverse the leverage.
The author reads the sale-leaseback at a 7.0% cap rate as a sign that Amazon prefers renting its buildings to issuing more bonds.
QTS placed only $300M of $800M of debt while BXDC committed $1.9B of equity to the Amazon deal.
Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close, its first quarter without Jensen, listed as a catalyst for AI financing sentiment.

sector_views.sector: Data center real estate and AI credit
sector_views.rationale: Finished, leased and guaranteed buildings find buyers, while development and refinancing risk persists as spreads widen and insurers and junk buyers step back.

earnings_insights: BXDC Q3 report (10-Q filed Nov 16): zero revenue, zero data centers, $1.96B cash and $28.2M interest income since the May IPO, with fees waived through Nov. 15.
BXDC's earnings call was scheduled for 9:00am ET Nov 16, with the mortgage rate and the identity of lenders as the key items.
Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close (Nov 17), its first quarter without Jensen. No estimates given.

risk_factors: Mortgage financing risk: $2.5B of non-recourse mortgages still need to be placed with life insurers and asset managers who told QTS they were full.
Leverage reversal if mortgage costs reach about 245bps over Treasuries.
Single-tenant, single-guarantor concentration, with two sites and 50% leverage.
Deal closing risk: Dec. 31 outside date and a $150M break fee.
Community opposition, state and local moratoria and regulatory action against data centers, per Blackstone's own risk factors.
More than 60% of 2027 planned data center capacity has not broken ground (JPMorgan, May).
Demand concentration if the shells serve Anthropic, with its IPO pricing Wednesday (author's unconfirmed inference).
Goldman downside risks to project finance forecast: construction delays, tighter economics, potential moratoria.
cross_bank_references: Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam on AI-related supply and off-balance-sheet liabilities.
JPMorgan report from May: more than 60% of capacity planned for completion in 2027 has not broken ground.
Bernstein project database: Amazon has the largest credible pipeline, 33 gigawatts.

tension_points.bull_case: The 2.75% rent escalator on the whole building becomes roughly 5% growth for equity if the debt is fixed. Finished, leased, AA-guaranteed buildings find buyers, and Blackstone has lender commitments.
tension_points.bear_case: A one-tenant REIT yielding 6.6% competes with a 5.15% 10-year Treasury and a hiking Fed, and the $2.5B of mortgages is five times what QTS could not place.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Mortgage pricing near 245bps over Treasuries, which the author says would make debt cost more than the buildings yield.

tension_points.bull_case: Capital is shifting into structured formats, with Goldman raising its 2027 AI project finance forecast to $545B and the Amazon deal showing the channel works.
tension_points.bear_case: AI issuer spreads are about 140bps against under 100bps for others, buyers of junk and IG paper are stepping back, and more than 60% of 2027 capacity has not broken ground.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak result at Thursday's 2:00pm ET bids on a $500 million data center loan auction, which includes $175 million tied to QTS.

theme_stances.key_argument: Amazon would rather rent its own buildings at 7% than add another bond, which signals funding stress in the AI buildout.
theme_stances.evidence: the best balance sheet in the business would rather rent its own buildings at 7%

theme_stances.key_argument: QTS placed only $300M of $800M, and insurers, junk funds and banks have stepped back from data center paper.
theme_stances.evidence: the lenders told the largest landlord in AI they'd had enough
